Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
1239 PM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* A potent winter storm continues to impact the region through 
  Friday morning, bringing heavy Sierra snow, strong winds, and 
  hazardous travel.

* Strong winds will continue over Sierra ridges, with gusty winds
  across western Nevada valleys and northeast California.

* A brief break in precipitation Friday afternoon through Saturday
  morning will be followed by another system arriving Saturday
  afternoon, with yet another system on Thanksgiving week.

&&

.DISCUSSION... 

* Periods of snow and heavy snow continues today in the Sierra,
  northeast CA, and western NV as the main upper level low and
  surface cold front move into the area. Current radar imagery as
  of 12 PM is showing widespread moderate to heavy snow showers in
  the Sierra, and light to locally moderate snow showers in
  western NV and northeast CA. For today, additional daytime snow
  accumulations are between 1-2 feet in the eastern Sierra at the
  crests, with a 70% chance for at least 12 inches on the crests.
  For lake level, additional amounts are between 2-6 inches. For 
  western NV and northeast CA, additional snow amounts up to 2" on
  the valley floors and 2-6" above 5,000 feet. Snow showers 
  become more isolated by the late evening.

* For Friday, high resolution models show a short-wave that will
  pivot around the main upper low. This feature will lead to snow
  showers through late Friday morning in the Sierra (mainly Tahoe
  area) and possibly western NV north of the Reno area. Additional
  accumulations Friday morning are up to 2-3" in the Sierra and up
  to 1" for western NV. There also remains the possibility of lake
  effect snowfall on the south/southeast portions of Pyramid Lake
  and Lake Tahoe later this evening into early Friday morning. It
  will be cold Friday morning, with widespread low to mid-20s in
  western NV to teens in the Sierra. Keep that in mind for the
  morning commute as slush on the roads may turn to ice. Friday
  will be cold, with temperatures around 15 degrees below average.
  By Saturday morning, we are looking at low teens in western NV
  to single digit readings in the Sierra.

* The next system to move through the region is from late Saturday
  night through early Monday morning. This system is weaker
  compared to our current storm. Snow accumulations are between
  3-6" along the Sierra crest and up to 3" above 6000 ft. The cold
  air in place will keep snow levels at or below valley floors,
  where a trace to 1" is possible for the Greater Reno area and
  other W NV communities by Monday morning. This system will
  maintain this streak of cold winter-like temperatures into the
  start of next week.

* The weather pattern remains unsettled for next week into
  Thanksgiving with additional storms bringing impacts to holiday
  travel. But, details and confidence is low at this time.
  -McKellar

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: Periods of -SN/SN continue through 00-02Z this 
evening. The heaviest snow band just passed late this morning. 
Activity becomes more showery and intermittent in the through the 
afternoon. Periods of MVFR to IFR are likely with the strongest 
showers through 12-15Z Friday. There is a 10-40% chance of 1 inch of 
snow or more by Friday morning. Winds will be generally light and 
VRB, except for W/NW winds with occasional gusts to 20 kts between 
20-02Z. Turbulence and LLWS persist through the evening.

Regional Outlook: Periods of SN/+SN continue through 12-15Z Friday 
for KTRK/KTVL/KMMH. An additional 6-12" of snow is possible on those 
locations. For KCXP/KMEV, periods of -SN/SN persist through the same 
timeframe with an additional 1-2". Gusts to 20-25 kts are possible 
especially between 23-04Z. Turbulence and LLWS persist through the 
evening.

24-72 Hour Outlook: Heavy mountain snow and valley rain/snow showers 
taper off by Friday morning. The next system approaches on Saturday 
afternoon and evening bringing more periods of valley rain and snow.

-HC

&&

.AVALANCHE...

An early season winter storm system will bring heavy snow to all 
avalanche center terrain through late tonight into Friday AM. 

* Snowfall Totals and Rates: An additional 2-6" of snow tonight
  into late Friday morning for the Sierra, including lake level in
  Tahoe. Snowfall rates during this time are between 0.5-1.0 
  inches per hour.
 
* SWE, SLRs, and Snow Levels: Along the crest, additional SWE of
  0.10 to 0.40 inches with a trace to 0.20" at lake level. SLRs 
  will be relatively high at 11-13:1, and locally up to 14:1. Snow
  levels remain below 6000 feet for the duration of the storm.

* Ridgetop Wind Gusts and Thunder: West winds gusting upwards of
  50-60 mph tonight through Friday morning. A 5% chance for
  thunder along the Sierra Crest Friday afternoon. -McKellar
